edition.title: Morning Edition
edition.dek: Spain's rail disaster; Haiti's deepening hunger; a disputed Sudan market strike; and Costa Rica's trade reversal.

lead_story.headline: At least 68 killed in Spain's second deadly high-speed rail disaster this year
lead_story.summary: Two trains on the Madrid–Seville line collided near Urda, Toledo, on October 28 after a signalling failure and a disputed decision to resume traffic. Regional authorities reported at least 68 deaths. Investigators are examining the control-room instructions; no final cause has been established.
lead_story.why_it_matters: The second major Spanish high-speed rail tragedy in 2026 raises urgent questions about how automated safety systems, manual overrides and railway oversight interact.
lead_story.source: El País — Liliana Ochoa and Spanish rail reporting

items.headline: New assessment finds 5.94 million people in Haiti face acute food insecurity
items.summary: A UN-backed food-security assessment estimates 5.94 million Haitians in crisis-level hunger or worse for September 2026–February 2027, including 1.8 million in the emergency category. Gang violence, displacement, high prices and rainfall deficits compound one another; the outlook for spring 2027 is worse.
items.why_it_matters: More than half the assessed population lacks dependable access to sufficient food. The problem is not only food supply but insecurity that prevents farming, transport and humanitarian delivery.

items.headline: Nyala market strike kills civilians as competing Sudan death tolls remain unresolved
items.summary: A drone strike hit the Tangoj night market in Nyala, South Darfur, on October 26. Sudanese medical sources report at least 21 deaths; a rights group alleges more than 100, while Médecins Sans Frontières says 36 bodies reached a supported hospital and more than 150 injured people were treated. These counts are not interchangeable or independently settled.
items.why_it_matters: An attack where civilians were trading near fighters illustrates the growing danger of drone warfare in Sudan and the difficulty of establishing reliable casualty counts amid restricted access.

items.headline: Costa Rica abandons Pacific trade pact bid and removes trade minister
items.summary: President Laura Fernández ordered Costa Rica to stop its accession process to the 12-member CPTPP and dismissed trade minister Indiana Trejos on October 28. She argued the negotiated terms had not been adequately shared with affected sectors; agricultural producer groups had protested the deal.
items.why_it_matters: The reversal exposes the domestic political trade-offs behind global trade integration, particularly when export opportunities collide with concerns about farmers and transparency.

items.headline: Recent miss: US and Japan announce plans for joint missile production in Japan
items.summary: Japan's defense minister Shinjiro Koizumi announced a plan for a Japanese facility to jointly produce advanced air-to-air missiles with the United States after talks in Cebu alongside regional defense meetings. The announcement describes a planned production capability, not a completed factory.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal would deepen industrial cooperation between two treaty allies and reflects how Indo-Pacific deterrence increasingly depends on ammunition supply and manufacturing capacity.

items.headline: Older catch-up: simple phone tutoring protected learning across five countries
items.summary: Five randomized trials published September 9 found that short, targeted phone tutorials improved primary-school numeracy during school disruptions in India, Kenya, Nepal, the Philippines and Uganda. Text messages alone produced mixed results; phone-based tutoring worked under both NGO and government delivery models.
items.why_it_matters: The durable lesson is that effective teaching design can matter more than sophisticated technology, particularly where internet access is limited or schools are closed.
items.source: Nature — Angrist, Ainomugisha, Bathena and colleagues

items.headline: A narwhal's spiral tusk is built from microscopic structures twisting in opposite directions
items.summary: Imaging across scales reveals that the outward left-handed helix of a narwhal tusk emerges from mineralized collagen patterns: the outer cementum twists one way, while inner dentine contains an opposing arrangement. The study was published in August, not this week.
items.why_it_matters: The result is an elegant example of how biological materials organize complex large-scale forms from microscopic architecture, without resolving every question about the tusk's evolutionary function.
items.source: Nature Communications — Rodriguez-Palomo, Vibe and colleagues

items.headline: In Johannesburg, neighbors learn to garden together at a once-neglected house
items.summary: At 12 Park Lane in Parktown, sisters Molemo and Pelonomi Moiloa helped turn an overgrown property into a community garden. Monthly open days bring neighbors together to prune, plant, weed, share a harvest and catch up; the project began with a street clean-up involving about 50 people.
items.why_it_matters: A small, specific view of urban community life in South Africa: shared space becomes a routine built through neighbors' work rather than a headline-making intervention.
items.source: Johannesburg In Your Pocket — Unathi Nkhoma

items.headline: Why competition in games depends on a shared agreement to cooperate
items.summary: Game designer Eric Zimmerman argues that play's conflicts are unusual: rivals consent to a common framework that makes struggle meaningful. Drawing on Gregory Bateson, Jean Piaget and Bernie De Koven, he asks how rules, role-playing and shared trust allow competition to teach social cooperation.
items.why_it_matters: The argument distinguishes constructive disagreement from hostility and suggests that the quality of a game depends as much on how people play together as on who wins.

worth_your_time.headline: How a 1607 flood became a warning from heaven in Britain's early news culture
worth_your_time.summary: Erik Crnkovich reads seventeenth-century pamphlets about the Bristol Channel flood to show how a real catastrophe became material for religious warning, political interpretation and sensational print. The essay separates the flood's history from the stories printers used to make it meaningful.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: A compelling history of how people interpreted disaster before modern meteorology—and of the old problems of evidence, incentives and audience attention in a new medium.
worth_your_time.source: The Public Domain Review — Erik Crnkovich

https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-28/que.standfirst: Spain's rail tragedy is a failure to understand in detail, not a verdict already reached.
body: The collision occurred after a failure in the LZB safety system interrupted trains on the Madrid–Seville corridor. Reporting from Spain indicates that controllers shifted to manual instructions and that a Renfe train was allowed to resume while an Iryo train remained stopped ahead.

El País and RTVE report at least 68 fatalities by the evening of October 28. Rescue and identification were continuing, so this is a provisional count. The number of passengers and injured people varies across early reports; the most reliable comparison is the official updated death toll, not a blended total.

The key investigative question is how a system designed to maintain train separation handled degraded signalling. Investigators will need recorded instructions, train telemetry, signal logs and the precise sequence of warnings; the transport minister's criticism of the control-room decision is not a substitute for the formal investigation.

Spain experienced another deadly high-speed rail collision in January 2026, but authorities have not established that the two incidents share a cause. A second accident increases pressure for a systemic safety review without proving a common technical defect.
https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-28/que.why_it_matters: Passengers depend on layers of safety that must remain effective when automated controls fail and humans take over.
https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-28/que.background: High-speed networks combine automated train protection, dispatching rules, driver instructions and emergency procedures. A fault in one layer should not automatically defeat the others.
https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-28/que.bigger_picture: The larger issue is whether organizations test and enforce safe degraded-mode operations, rather than treating an individual operator's action as the entire explanation.

significance.label: Major development
significance.rationale: A large loss of life with immediate implications for transport oversight and public confidence.

https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-28/que.uncertainty: Investigators have not established final causal responsibility. Early accounts differ on injury totals, timing and whether instructions were misunderstood or improperly issued.
key_points: The reported LZB failure preceded the collision.
A stopped train remained ahead when traffic resumed.
A formal inquiry must reconstruct the control-room and driver decisions.
what_to_watch: Official investigation findings and published train-control logs
Reconciled casualty and injury counts
Independent safety audit recommendations

supporting_sources.name: Associated Press — Spanish train crash investigation
RTVE — Sánchez pledges investigation at Urda

https://apnews.com/article/e7054f6124e38.standfirst: The new food-security numbers are a measurement of households' access to food, not a claim that famine has been declared everywhere.
body: The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) estimates 5.94 million people in Haiti at Phase 3 or worse during September 2026–February 2027. Of those, 1.8 million are in Phase 4, an emergency category. A separate projection puts 6.35 million in Phase 3 or worse for March–June 2027.

Phase 3 means families face significant food-consumption gaps or must use damaging coping strategies to eat. Phase 4 is more severe. These categories are not identical to a formal area-wide famine classification, which requires additional mortality and malnutrition criteria.

Armed groups interrupt road transport and force people from farms and homes. High food and fuel costs reduce purchasing power, while rainfall deficits threaten production. These factors reinforce each other: more food in the country does not help families who cannot safely reach markets.

The IPC is a joint technical assessment rather than a household-by-household census. Earlier reporting by Haiti's Le Nouvelliste documented a worsening food-security picture in April; the latest numerical estimate comes from IPC, independently discussed by AP and supported by FEWS NET's September analysis.
https://apnews.com/article/e7054f6124e38.why_it_matters: The severity is nationwide and structural: insecurity, farming disruption and inaccessible markets undermine even well-designed food assistance.
https://apnews.com/article/e7054f6124e38.background: IPC uses standardized categories to compare food-security severity and forecast likely outcomes. Its projections are conditional on conflict, weather and assistance assumptions.
https://apnews.com/article/e7054f6124e38.bigger_picture: Humanitarian relief is necessary, but secure agricultural production and transport are also essential for durable recovery.

significance.label: Major development
significance.rationale: The assessment indicates crisis-level hunger for over half the analyzed population.

https://apnews.com/article/e7054f6124e38.uncertainty: These are modeled and surveyed estimates, not exact headcounts. The projection may change with conflict intensity, harvests and funding. A new independent Haitian on-the-ground report for the October release was not confirmed during this search.
key_points: 5.94 million are assessed at crisis level or worse.
1.8 million are in the emergency category.
The projected March–June 2027 total is higher, not a current observed count.
what_to_watch: Updated IPC/FEWS NET assessments
Safe humanitarian access and market functioning
Changes in displacement, rainfall and harvest conditions

supporting_sources.name: Le Nouvelliste — Haitian reporting on April CNSA results

https://sudantribune.com/article/320577.standfirst: Nyala's market was struck; how many people died, and who precisely was targeted, remain contested.
body: Sudan Tribune reported a strike on the Tangoj night market in Nyala on October 26, where traders and shoppers mixed with members of the Rapid Support Forces. Local medical reporting put the toll at at least 21 dead and more than 40 wounded, while other monitors offered substantially higher figures.

Médecins Sans Frontières reported 36 bodies received at Nyala Teaching Hospital and more than 150 people treated for injuries. Emergency Lawyers alleged more than 100 deaths. Hospital arrivals are a concrete medical observation but cannot establish the total killed across all sites.

Associated Press interviewed witnesses describing civilian vendors selling food or tea near fighters, and also reported the army-aligned account of a strike on RSF recruits. The presence of combatants does not erase the obligation to distinguish civilians and take precautions.

Repeated drone strikes on markets, homes and power infrastructure have expanded the war's civilian toll. Communications failures and unsafe access make independent forensic reconstruction unusually difficult.
https://sudantribune.com/article/320577.why_it_matters: Accurate casualty reporting matters for accountability, but the uncertainty must not conceal confirmed civilian suffering.
https://sudantribune.com/article/320577.background: Sudan's army and RSF have fought since 2023. Nyala is controlled by the RSF; civilian markets and economic activity continue alongside military movements.
https://sudantribune.com/article/320577.bigger_picture: Remote warfare can blur the distinction between military gatherings and civilian livelihoods, especially where people depend on selling goods near armed groups.

significance.label: Major development
significance.rationale: Credible independent medical evidence establishes a serious mass-casualty event, even though totals diverge.

https://sudantribune.com/article/320577.uncertainty: The casualty figures reflect different evidence bases and reporting times. Responsibility and target characterization are disputed; the army-aligned statement is a participant's claim, not independent proof.
key_points: Sudan Tribune supplies local accounts of the market strike.
MSF directly reports hospital arrivals.
AP corroborates civilian vendors' presence while preserving uncertainty.
what_to_watch: Reconciled hospital and burial records
Independent investigation of the target and weapon
Civilian protection measures and humanitarian access

supporting_sources.name: Médecins Sans Frontières — Nyala hospital account
Associated Press — eyewitness and competing accounts

https://www.nacion.com/economia/laura-fe.standfirst: Costa Rica's trade reversal concerns the political legitimacy of a negotiation as much as its economic merits.
body: President Laura Fernández said the CPTPP terms were not sufficiently disclosed to affected sectors and removed trade minister Indiana Trejos. Costa Rican newspaper La Nación reported the dismissal and instruction not to sign, while Reuters independently confirmed the withdrawal.

The CPTPP is a large trade arrangement connecting economies across the Pacific and beyond. Costa Rica had pursued accession since 2022 and received an invitation to join in 2024, so the reversal ends a lengthy diplomatic process rather than a preliminary inquiry.

Producer groups, particularly in agriculture, had raised concerns about exposure to foreign competition. Those objections are relevant to domestic distribution of gains and losses, but they do not establish that the overall economic agreement would have been harmful.

The administration's complaint about secrecy is its stated rationale. The final negotiating documents and a detailed public cost-benefit assessment would be needed to evaluate the transparency claim and the economic trade-off independently.
https://www.nacion.com/economia/laura-fe.why_it_matters: The decision may alter export opportunities and sets a precedent for how governments consult domestic sectors during trade talks.
https://www.nacion.com/economia/laura-fe.background: Accession to a trade pact involves negotiations on tariffs, market access and regulatory obligations, often over several administrations.
https://www.nacion.com/economia/laura-fe.bigger_picture: The broader tension is between long-term integration and domestic consent, especially when the benefits are diffuse but costs are concentrated.

significance.label: Meaningful signal
significance.rationale: A consequential policy reversal in a country previously advancing toward a major trade bloc.

https://www.nacion.com/economia/laura-fe.uncertainty: The president's explanation is not independent proof of procedural wrongdoing. The minister's full response and negotiated texts were not established in the reviewed reporting.
key_points: The accession bid was stopped on October 28.
The trade minister was removed.
Agricultural concerns and alleged secrecy are part of the public dispute.
what_to_watch: Publication of the negotiated terms
Appointment of a replacement minister
Alternative Costa Rican trade strategy

supporting_sources.name: Reuters — independent report on Costa Rica's CPTPP withdrawal

https://apnews.com/article/3351555ce9c46.standfirst: Japan and the United States have announced an industrial-defense plan; the factory is not yet operating.
body: After meeting in Cebu, Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi announced a plan to produce advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles jointly with the United States at a facility in Japan. AP reports the initiative as Operation Supercharge.

The talks took place alongside Southeast Asian defense meetings in the Philippines. ABS-CBN independently documented the Cebu gathering and US defense secretary's arrival, although that local coverage did not independently confirm the missile-factory details.

Joint production can reduce dependence on overseas supply chains and improve stockpiles, but announcement is different from a funded, built and operational production line. The cost, production schedule and technology-transfer arrangements are not yet established in the available reporting.

The development sits within Japan's growing defense-industrial cooperation with the United States and regional concerns about maritime security. Neither minister publicly identified a particular country as the project's target in the AP account.
https://apnews.com/article/3351555ce9c46.why_it_matters: Defense readiness depends on industrial throughput and logistics, not only platforms and treaty commitments.
https://apnews.com/article/3351555ce9c46.background: Advanced air-to-air missiles support modern fighter aircraft. Local production involves licensing, manufacturing, testing and procurement decisions.
https://apnews.com/article/3351555ce9c46.bigger_picture: Regional alliances increasingly pursue supply resilience alongside exercises and diplomatic statements.

significance.label: Meaningful signal
significance.rationale: A potentially durable shift in allied manufacturing capacity, contingent on implementation.

https://apnews.com/article/3351555ce9c46.uncertainty: Specific production commitments currently rest on AP's account of the Japanese minister's announcement. Local Philippine reporting confirms the meeting, not the industrial terms; a separately accessible Japanese primary release was not confirmed.
key_points: A joint production facility was proposed.
The meeting occurred alongside ASEAN defense diplomacy.
Production dates, scale and contracts remain open.
what_to_watch: Formal bilateral implementation documents
Japanese budget and factory location
First actual production milestones

supporting_sources.name: ABS-CBN — Cebu defense meeting arrival
supporting_sources.role: Local reporting — independently confirms meeting context

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-0.standfirst: Low-tech tutoring can outperform low-engagement remote education when the teaching is targeted.
body: Researchers coordinated five randomized trials in India, Kenya, Nepal, the Philippines and Uganda during COVID-era school disruptions. Children received either text-based support or short phone tutorials that assessed their current numeracy and taught at that level.

Across the five studies, phone tutoring plus SMS improved learning; SMS alone showed mixed and generally smaller effects. The pooled gain in numerical operations was about 0.32 standard deviations for the phone-and-SMS treatment.

In Nepal and the Philippines, both government teachers and NGO instructors improved outcomes, addressing a frequent concern that small NGO pilots do not translate to public systems. The authors estimate an average cost of about $11 per child, but cost-effectiveness depends on local delivery assumptions.

The pedagogical mechanism matters: the calls were not merely friendly check-ins. They combined regular assessment with instruction matched to the child's level. The study's comparison with less-targeted remote lessons suggests that using a phone is not itself the cause of learning gains.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-0.why_it_matters: The research provides a tested contingency model for schooling interrupted by conflict, climate disasters or epidemics.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-0.background: Random assignment helps isolate effects of the intervention. The trials studied specific populations and pandemic disruptions, not every school system.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-0.bigger_picture: The most scalable educational technology may be a basic telephone coupled with good teaching and reliable monitoring.

significance.label: Important context
significance.rationale: Multi-country randomized evidence with practical implications for education resilience.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-0.uncertainty: Learning gains varied by country and implementation; generalization to different ages, subjects or long-term outcomes remains uncertain. Authors' cost estimates are model-dependent.
key_points: Five randomized trials across different countries.
Targeted calls worked more consistently than texts alone.
Government delivery produced measurable gains in studied settings.
what_to_watch: Independent replication outside pandemic closures
Learning retention over years
Government implementation quality at national scale

supporting_sources.name: What Works Hub — implementation science in education

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-0.standfirst: The famous left-handed tusk contains a more complicated microscopic twist.
body: The study combined structural techniques to examine narwhal tusks from mineralized collagen fibrils up to the visible spiral. The outer cementum exhibits a left-handed helical arrangement, while the inner dentine shows an opposing right-handed pattern.

The result explains how an overall left-handed form can emerge from nested structures whose directions differ. This is a materials-architecture finding, not a demonstration that the twist is produced by the narwhal consciously rotating its head.
Narwhal tusks are elongated teeth, most commonly developed in males. They have long been associated with unicorn myths and debated biological functions, including social or sexual signaling.
The paper is a durable August discovery selected for its unusual insight into multiscale structure; it is not breaking news. Independent research summaries describe the same measured architecture.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-0.why_it_matters: The research helps connect biological form to microscopic material arrangement, with potential relevance to biomimetic design.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-0.background: Chirality describes handedness: two otherwise similar spiral arrangements can turn in opposite directions.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-0.bigger_picture: Complex biological structures can arise from interactions among layers rather than one uniformly oriented material.

significance.label: Interesting discovery
significance.rationale: A well-defined and counterintuitive finding about biological materials.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-0.uncertainty: The paper does not settle all evolutionary functions of the tusk or demonstrate an engineering application.
key_points: Outer cementum and inner dentine show opposite handedness.
Multiscale imaging links microscopic and macroscopic form.
The evolutionary role of the tusk remains debated.
what_to_watch: Replication in more tusks and populations
Mechanical tests of the layered architecture
Whether similar arrangements occur in other tissues

https://psyche.co/ideas/a-game-is-not-a-.standfirst: How can two people struggle against each other while still collaborating?
body: Zimmerman's central thesis is that games create a special form of conflict that requires consent to a shared framework. Competition is not simply the absence of cooperation; it is often a cooperative activity in which people jointly sustain a contest.

First, players agree to treat certain goals and obstacles as meaningful. Second, they voluntarily accept rules that make those obstacles intelligible. Third, they can compete intensely while recognizing that the opponent is a participant rather than an enemy. The conclusion is that the conflict's meaning depends on shared play.

Gregory Bateson's example of animals play-biting helps clarify the distinction between an action and its play-frame: the nip resembles aggression while signaling that it is not a real fight. The same layered awareness lets people immerse themselves in games without losing sight of their constructed nature.

Zimmerman then draws on Jean Piaget's study of children's marbles: younger players treat rules as fixed, while older children can recognize them as agreements that a group can revise. Bernie De Koven extends this insight by asking whether changing a rule can improve the experience for everyone.

Consider two friends playing chess. Each tries to defeat the other, yet both protect the activity by honoring turns and legal moves. If one cheats or harasses the other, the opponent may still lose pieces, but the jointly created game deteriorates. This is Morning Edition's illustrative example, not a quotation from Zimmerman.

A strong objection is that some games involve coercive structures, unequal access or hostile incentives. Voluntary agreement can be partial, and a player may be pressured to continue. Zimmerman's discussion of toxic play acknowledges that the cooperative frame is fragile; it does not prove that every competitive system is healthy.

If the thesis is useful, designing and moderating games means caring for the conditions of shared participation, not only victory. It also invites a broader question about institutions: when does adversarial competition remain productive because all parties still value the common rules?
https://psyche.co/ideas/a-game-is-not-a-.why_it_matters: Competition can train social trust and perspective-taking, but only when the participants can still recognize a shared activity.
https://psyche.co/ideas/a-game-is-not-a-.background: The essay draws on Bateson's theory of play signals, Piaget's moral development research, De Koven's play community and studies of role-playing identities.
https://psyche.co/ideas/a-game-is-not-a-.bigger_picture: Play offers a model of disagreement where opponents can be collaborators in sustaining the contest. Whether politics or markets share this feature requires separate argument.

significance.label: Worth thinking about
significance.rationale: A clear philosophical framework for understanding games as social practices.

https://psyche.co/ideas/a-game-is-not-a-.uncertainty: The strongest objection is whether consent and shared rules really characterize all games, especially games involving exploitation, exclusion or unequal power. The broader institutional analogy is interpretive rather than empirically proven.
key_points: A game creates a voluntary shared rule-frame.
Conflict within the frame can be cooperative.
Rules can be negotiated and redesigned.
Abuse can break the shared play-frame.
what_to_watch: Where does competition stop being consensual?
Who gets to revise the rules?
Can adversarial institutions retain a common good?
connections: Piaget on children's understanding of rules
De Koven on communities of players

https://publicdomainreview.org/essay/won.standfirst: Seventeenth-century disaster reporting was already entangled with belief, profit and contested credibility.
body: Crnkovich begins with the Bristol Channel flood of January 1607, a real catastrophe that later historians estimate killed around 2,000 people. Pamphleteers quickly produced accounts of ruined villages, drowned livestock and extraordinary rescues.

Their reporting was not simply descriptive. Writers interpreted the flood as divine punishment, a warning to repent or evidence of providential mercy. The same episode could be made to support theological and political claims.

The essay explores a growing print market hungry for marvels: floods, strange apparitions, unusual weather and supposed miracles. Some pamphlets emphasized named witnesses to establish credibility, while others relied on dramatic claims or literary devices.

Crnkovich does not ask us to treat the reported miracles as verified events. The distinction is between a disaster, contemporaneous beliefs about it, and the incentives of people selling printed narratives. Readers at the time were not necessarily credulous; some pamphleteers defended themselves against accusations of unreliable reporting.

The historical setting matters. Religious division after the Reformation made providential explanations politically charged, while an emerging market for cheap print rewarded dramatic, emotionally resonant stories. The essay's most useful connection to today is not that modern media is identical, but that evidence and interpretation were already being mixed in public accounts.
https://publicdomainreview.org/essay/won.why_it_matters: It illuminates how the media's commercial form and a society's dominant ideas influence what a catastrophe is said to mean.
https://publicdomainreview.org/essay/won.background: Early modern broadsides and pamphlets reached audiences beyond elite manuscript culture. Natural phenomena could be read simultaneously as physical events and moral signs.
https://publicdomainreview.org/essay/won.bigger_picture: Modern readers can distinguish empirical evidence from the meaning-making frameworks imposed on it without assuming earlier readers were incapable of skepticism.

significance.label: Important context
significance.rationale: A carefully sourced historical essay that changes how we think about the history of news.

https://publicdomainreview.org/essay/won.uncertainty: Pamphlets are evidence of claims and beliefs, not direct verification of every anecdote. Historical casualty estimates and weather explanations are reconstructed from incomplete records.
key_points: The flood was real; not every pamphlet story is established.
Providential interpretations served religious and political functions.
Early print markets had incentives for sensationalism.
Contemporaries also debated credibility.
what_to_watch: What counts as evidence when a story is emotionally compelling?
How does the business model of a medium shape its interpretations?

supporting_sources.name: The Public Domain Review — primary historical pamphlets and bibliography
